question: What historical Agusan Marsh evidence does Munda and Estaño (2020) provide for Nile tilapia, and can the study support diet, precise locality, or current-presence claims?

source.citation: Munda, L. C., & Estaño, L. A. (2020). Infection of Acanthocephalan Parasite Acanthogyrus sp. in Nile Tilapia Oreochromis niloticus Collected from Agusan Marsh, Philippines. Journal of Ecosystem Science and Eco-Governance, 2(1), 25-31.
source.fullTextProvenance: The Caraga State University journal's official article PDF was retrieved and reviewed; no PDF, figure or table copy is retained in this repository.

licenseReview.articlePageStatement: The official article page names Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International (CC BY-NC 4.0).
licenseReview.pdfFrontMatterStatement: The PDF front matter uses a generic Creative Commons Attribution License statement without naming a version; extracted PDF text also contains a CC BY NC marker.
licenseReview.decision: Follow the more restrictive item-page CC BY-NC 4.0 statement for this review. Do not adapt or publish the article's figures or tables in Bangwit without a qualified, item-specific rights determination.

source.studyArea: Agusan Marsh, Caraga Region; six named municipality-level collection areas: Bunawan, San Francisco, Rosario, Talacogon, La Paz and Loreto.

sampling.reportedAllocation: Thirty fish per each of six sampling stations/municipality-level areas, for 180 total.
sampling.samplingPeriod: December 2019-January 2020; the article says collection was done once at each sampling site.
sampling.selection: Semi-purposive selection based on site accessibility and availability of fresh O. niloticus.
sampling.studyMethod: The study measured fish length and weight and examined the intestine for adult acanthocephalan parasites using microscopy. It was not a stomach-content or diet-composition study.
sampling.siteResolution: No station coordinates, voucher numbers or exact sample-to-coordinate table were found in the reviewed full text. The map is illustrative and was not digitized.

findings.historicalCaptureEvidence: The source reports direct collection of O. niloticus from six Agusan Marsh municipality-level areas in late 2019 and early 2020; this is historical capture evidence, not current monitoring.
findings.parasiteFinding: The authors report Acanthogyrus sp. in sampled fish and 81 infected hosts out of 180 in the results. Parasite identification is reported at genus level; the article recommends molecular and ultrastructural follow-up.
internalReportingIssues: The abstract reports San Francisco prevalence as 76%, while the results text and figure report 76.7%.
The abstract describes site-prevalence significance as p<0.05, while the results text reports p<0.001.
The Figure 3 caption says Asinan Marsh although the title, abstract, methods and nearby text identify Agusan Marsh.
The methods/body spell Talacogon as Talagocon in one passage, while the abstract and acknowledgements use Talacogon.
findings.dietBoundary: No food items or gut contents were identified. Discussion statements about possible intermediate hosts, foraging or parasite transmission are hypotheses/citations, not measured tilapia diet evidence and not bait guidance.
findings.waterQualityBoundary: Differences in parasite prevalence are discussed as possibly related to water quality, but this study did not report water-quality measurements; it cannot support a current contamination or fish-safety warning.

decision.reason: This is useful historical direct-capture evidence for one reported fish taxon across six broad collection areas, but the sampling sites lack coordinates/vouchers, the map caption and several result values conflict, the parasite identity remains genus-level, and the publisher page restricts reuse to noncommercial. It is not a diet study or current safety assessment.

limitations: The purposive and access-dependent sampling is a 2019-2020 snapshot rather than a representative estimate for all Agusan Marsh or Caraga waters.
The six municipality labels do not define exact fishing stations or geometry, and no specimen accessions were reported in the reviewed text.
Oreochromis niloticus is the paper's identification; no independent specimen or genetic re-identification was performed.
Acanthogyrus is reported only to genus and the article itself recommends molecular/ultrastructural confirmation.
The publication page's CC BY-NC 4.0 notice differs from the PDF's generic attribution wording; no app reuse is approved.
No diet, bait, present-day occurrence, population abundance, water-quality status, contamination level, legal catchability or public-app row was added.
nextAction: Continue Caraga freshwater source review. Treat this as a dated, municipality-level tilapia collection lead only; seek separate direct diet and station-resolved sources, and keep public use pending rights and evidence review.

references.supports: Official publisher full text: sample design, study methods, site labels, parasite results and map-caption discrepancy.
Official article page: metadata, abstract, publication date, citation and item-specific CC BY-NC 4.0 license notice.
Official issue record and issue publication date.
